The petitioners have filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against respondents seeking compensation on account of death of one Sri.K.V.Govindaraju S/o Venkataramanappa, who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
On 06-07-2023 the said K.V.Govindaraju was standing by the side of Chintamani - Hosakote Road to cross the road, on the way at about 08.10 p.m, one Motor Cycle bearing No.AP-04-AT-4667 came from Hosakote side, at high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and came to the wrong side of the road and dashed violently against K.V.Govindaraju.
Due to heavy impact, he fell down and sustained grievous head injuries and became unconscious on the spot.

Immediately after the accident he was shifted to Silicon City hospital, Hosakote, wherein after first aid treatment, he was referred to Manipal hospital, Bengaluru, wherein severe traumatic brain injury with brainstem dysfunction was noticed and treated at MICU.

In the course of treatment he succumbed to the injuries on 08.07.2023 and petitioners have spent (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.5178/2023 Rs.6,00,000/- towards treatment, medicines,
conveyance etc., and spent Rs.50,000/- towards transportation of deadbody and funeral obsequies.

Prior to accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 48 years and was doing agriculture and doing Timber business by profession and earning Rs.50,000/- p.m and petitioners were entirely depending upon the earnings of the deceased.

Due to sudden demise of the deceased, the petitioners are Gayathri S vs Obanna T on 5 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87246004/
2 put to lot of mental agony and untold misery.

The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of offending Motor Cycle by its rider and in this regard the Hosakote Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of offending Motor Cycle.

The respondent No.1 being the RC owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending Motor Cycle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- to the petitioners with cost and interest.

03. On service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared before the tribunal through their counsels, but only the respondent No.2 has filed objections and counsel for the respondent No.1 has filed Memo of retirement on 17.09.2025 stating that there has been no communication or contact from the (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.5178/2023 respondent No.1 and all attempts to contact him has failed.

04. Respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioners and further denied alleged accident, negligence of the rider of offending Motor Cycle, age, avocation,
income of the deceased, dependency of the petitioners with the deceased, nature of the injuries sustained by the deceased, treatment taken by the deceased and expenses incurred by the petitioners and admits that this respondent has issued policy of insurance in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of Motor Cycle bearing No.AP-04-AT-4667 and the liability of this respondent is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and contended that the rider of the said Motor Cycle was not holding a valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and respondent No.1 has contravened the provisions of M.V. Act and also committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.

The alleged accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the deceased only, who while trying to cross the busy main road, who without observing the traffic unmindfully suddenly try to cross in a negligent manner and hit by some unknown Motor Cycle and caused the alleged accident.

As such the (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.5178/2023 accident took place due to the negligence on the part of the deceased alone and he is the tort-feasor for the same, not due to the negligence on the part of the rider of offending Motor Cycle and there is no nexus between the injury and death.
The compensation claimed is highly excessive, exaggerated and pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2.

towards treatment, medicines, conveyance etc., and spent Rs.50,000/- towards transportation of deadbody and funeral obsequies.

13. It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The petitioners have not produced any birth certificate, school records and SSLC marks card of the deceased to show his exact date of birth.
However, they have produced Ex.P.14 Aadhaar card of deceased.

Eventhough the said document is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of other evidence regarding age, said documents can be relied upon and according to which (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.5178/2023 deceased date of birth is mentioned as 18.09.1974.
The alleged accident occurred on 06.07.2023 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased is 49 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased as 49 years as on the date of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 46 to 50 is "13".

sentences.text: Since deceased was aged about 49 years at the time of accident and was self employee and he comes in the age group of 40 to 50 years, 25% income should be added to the monthly income towards future prospects which would be result in the income to be (30,000 + 7,500) = Rs.37,500/-.

Since there are five dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the income of the deceased towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (37,500 - 9,375) = Rs.28,125/-.
The income of the deceased for the purpose of determining the loss of dependency would thus be Rs.28,125/-.
As the deceased was aged about 49 years, the multiplier of 13 would have to be applied.
Consequently the claimants would be entitled for a sum of Rs.43,87,500/- (Rs.28,125/- x 12 x 13) towards loss of dependency.

In view of the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s.
